_comment: Decisions on filings in the letters review queue, carried into every later queue by scripts/letters-queue.mjs. rejected: read and found not to be a letter (or a repeat, or too thin), with the reason. review: a genuine letter a person must finish (no readable text, or too thin to ground). A published filing is not listed: it leaves the queue because the catalogue holds it.

The only other genuine Elliott-campaign letter: the four nominees' (Coffman, Cornelius, Heim, Nieuwoudt) closing letter to Phillips 66 shareholders of 20 May 2025, reproduced in the press release in the DFAN14A cover document, not in the queued Exhibit 99.1 (social media posts and website materials, image-only). Distinct, but short and thin (about 500 words, no figures, no plan beyond a general call for change), so an editor should decide whether it meets the bar; if published, the source is the cover .htm and four new writers are needed.

Not written by the manager: Exhibit 1 is a reposted third-party opinion column (an Activist Spotlight piece by Kenneth Squire of 13D Monitor about Engaged Capital and BlackLine) posted to SaveBlackLine.com; most of its text is also unreadable (custom font encoding).

Genuine Starboard letter to the Tripadvisor chairman, CEO and board dated 17 February 2026, but the PDF is set in Type 3 fonts with no Unicode mapping, so pdftotext returns no readable text and no note or quote can be checked by script. Leave for a person (OCR or a reading by hand), as the catalogue does for image-only letters.
Repeat: the Exhibit 99.1 to Starboard's Schedule 13D/A is byte-identical to the letter filed the same day on DFAN14A (0000921895-26-000436). Dedupe to that one record.

Routine performance attribution: the unsigned section reports each of the four quarters' contributors and detractors with brief price explanations, and has no market view or statement of approach. It is a performance discussion, not a letter.

Too thin to be a letter: the unsigned 'To Our Stockholders' section is a returns paragraph, two paragraphs of macro recap (Iran conflict, the new Fed chairman) and two lines naming three contributors and three detractors with no reasoning. Routine report material.
